title: The quotient of a self-relation embeds in its target stack
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, their morphisms and 2-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. An algebraic stack is an fppf stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas [def-pc-fppf-site, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. A morphism is representable by algebraic spaces if every scheme base change is an algebraic space. For representable maps, flatness, local finite presentation and local finite type are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Surjectivity means that every field-valued target object lifts, up to isomorphism, after some field extension [def-weil-field]. Let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $S$, let $U$ be an algebraic space over $S$ and let $a:U\to\mathcal X$ be a morphism. Then $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$ is an algebraic space. The source and target projections, identities, inverse and composition of isomorphisms in $\mathcal X(T)$ make $(U,R)$ a groupoid in algebraic spaces: an arrow over $T$ is a triple $(u,v,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:a(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}a(v)$. Let $q:U\to[U/R]$ be the object map to its fppf stackification [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. There is a morphism $i:[U/R]\to\mathcal X$, with a specified 2-isomorphism $i q\simeq a$, which is fully faithful on each fibre groupoid over an $S$-scheme $T$. If $[U/R]$ is an algebraic stack, then $i$ is representable by algebraic spaces. Here fully faithful means bijective on all sets of arrows between two objects; in particular $i$ is a monomorphism in this sense.

proof.text: The diagonal of $\mathcal X$ is representable by hypothesis, so [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability] applied to $a:U\to\mathcal X$ makes $a$ representable by algebraic spaces. Apply [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space] with $\mathcal F=U$, $\mathcal G=\mathcal X$ and $Z=U$ to obtain the algebraic space $R$. Its test-scheme points are triples $(u,v,\alpha:a(u)\to a(v))$, by the 2-fibre-product definition [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; since $U$ is discrete there are no further identifications between such triples. Set $s(u,v,\alpha)=u$, $t(u,v,\alpha)=v$, $e(u)=(u,u,1)$, $j(u,v,\alpha)=(v,u,\alpha^{-1})$, and $c((u,v,\alpha),(v,w,\beta))=(u,w,\beta\alpha)$. These operations commute with pullback (using its canonical comparison isomorphisms), hence are natural transformations, thus morphisms of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Their laws are exactly identity, associativity and inverse laws in $\mathcal X(T)$.

Let $\mathcal P(T)$ have objects $U(T)$ and arrows the triples above. The functor $F:\mathcal P\to\mathcal X$ sends $u$ to $a(u)$ and $(u,v,\alpha)$ to $\alpha$; the displayed composition formula proves functoriality. The big fppf site is taken in the larger universe of the statement. Apply the extension clause of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] to $F$ and the fppf stack $\mathcal X$. It supplies $i:[U/R]\to\mathcal X$ and an invertible transformation $iq\cong a$.

For $u,v\in U(T)$, the arrow presheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal P}(u,v)$ is exactly $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X}(a(u),a(v))$, by the triple description. It is already an fppf sheaf, since $\mathcal X$ is a stack. The isomorphism-sheaf clause of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] identifies $\operatorname{Isom}(q(u),q(v))$ with its sheafification. The universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] makes the unit an isomorphism for an already sheaf: extend the identity to a retraction, and use uniqueness to show its other composite is the identity. Under $iq\cong a$, the map induced by $i$ composes with that unit to the identity of the original arrow sheaf, so it is its inverse. Thus $i$ induces the required bijections between arrows of original objects.

For arbitrary $b,c\in[U/R](T)$, choose a common fppf covering on which both are isomorphic to original objects, using the local-essential-image clause of [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. By Step 3 and conjugation with these isomorphisms, the map on their isomorphism sheaves is bijective on each cover member and every restriction of it. Given an arrow $i(b)\to i(c)$ over $T$, lift it uniquely on these members. The lifts agree on overlaps because their images agree and the local maps are injective. The sheaf condition for $\operatorname{Isom}(b,c)$ glues them to one arrow over $T$. Two global lifts are equal because their restrictions agree. This proves full faithfulness on every fibre, using only the two stack sheaf conditions and the local representatives.

Now assume $\mathcal Q=[U/R]$ is algebraic. Fix a scheme $T$ and $x\in\mathcal X(T)$. The discrete $h_T$ is an algebraic stack: [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space] supplies its fppf sheaf condition, its representable diagonal and identity atlas; the identity is smooth and surjective. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products], $\mathcal W=h_T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Q$ is algebraic. Over $V\to T$, an object is $(b,\phi:x|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}i(b))$. An arrow to $(c,\psi)$ must be an arrow $\gamma:b\to c$ with $i(\gamma)\phi=\psi$. Step 4 makes $\gamma$ uniquely determined (indeed it lifts $\psi\phi^{-1}$). Hence each fibre of $\mathcal W$ has at most one arrow between any two objects. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-setoid-space] to obtain an algebraic space representing $\mathcal W$. This works for every $T,x$, so it is exactly representability of $i$ by algebraic spaces. No algebraicity of $\mathcal Q$ was used before this step.

lean.statement: theorem self_relation_quotient_embedding {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)) (hX : IsAlgebraicModuliStack X) (U : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli U.obj.obj) X) : ∃ (R : AlgebraicSpace S) (s t : R.obj.obj ⟶ U.obj.obj) (e : U.obj.obj ⟶ R.obj.obj) (j : R.obj.obj ⟶ R.obj.obj) (c : pullback s t ⟶ R.obj.obj) (η : ModuliTwoIso ((discreteModuliMap s).comp a) ((discreteModuliMap t).comp a)), AlgebraicSpace.IsPresheafGroupoid s t e j c ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (x y : yoneda.obj T ⟶ U.obj.obj) (β : a.obj (CostructuredArrow.mk x) ⟶ a.obj (CostructuredArrow.mk y)), X.p.IsHomLift (𝟙 T) β → ∃! r : {r : yoneda.obj T ⟶ R.obj.obj // r ≫ s = x ∧ r ≫ t = y}, spaceGroupoidPresentationArrow s t a η x y r = β) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (x y z : yoneda.obj T ⟶ U.obj.obj) (r : {r : yoneda.obj T ⟶ R.obj.obj // r ≫ s = x ∧ r ≫ t = y}) (q : {q : yoneda.obj T ⟶ R.obj.obj // q ≫ s = y ∧ q ≫ t = z}) (d : {d : yoneda.obj T ⟶ R.obj.obj // d ≫ s = x ∧ d ≫ t = z}) (p : yoneda.obj T ⟶ pullback s t), p ≫ pullback.fst s t = q.val → p ≫ pullback.snd s t = r.val → p ≫ c = d.val → spaceGroupoidPresentationArrow s t a η x y r ≫ spaceGroupoidPresentationArrow s t a η y z q = spaceGroupoidPresentationArrow s t a η x z d) ∧ (∀ (Q : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over S)) (q : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli U.obj.obj) Q) (hQ : SpaceGroupoidQuotientPresentation s t e j c Q q), ∃ (i : BasedFunctor Q X) (θ : ModuliTwoIso (q.comp i) a), (∀ (T : Over S) (r : yoneda.obj T ⟶ R.obj.obj), i.map (hQ.arrows.val.hom.app (CostructuredArrow.mk r)) ≫ θ.val.hom.app (CostructuredArrow.mk (r ≫ t)) = θ.val.hom.app (CostructuredArrow.mk (r ≫ s)) ≫ η.val.hom.app (CostructuredArrow.mk r)) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (b d : Functor.Fiber Q.p T), Function.Bijective ((moduliFiberMap i T).map (X := b) (Y := d))) ∧ (IsAlgebraicModuliStack Q → IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces i))
lean.note: The self-relation is specified by its natural tautological isomorphism and unique vertical-arrow lifting on all test schemes, with composition fixed to composition in the target. The conclusion applies to any fppf quotient presentation, retaining the canonical arrow comparison and the specified two-isomorphism iq ≅ a. Algebraicity of the quotient is used only in the final conditional representability clause. Uses the existing groupoid, quotient-presentation, and algebraic-stack predicates; no new notion or statement correction.
